title: Introduction to Security
subtitle: Jeopardy Review

jeopardyFormatExample.clueText: This biometric authentication factor is an example of 'something you are'

categoryLegend: Physical Security: locks, badges, biometrics, mantrap, fire suppression.  Authentication & Access Control: CIA triad, MFA, RBAC, encryption.  Malware & Social Engineering: virus, worm, ransomware, phishing, vishing.  Wireless Security: WEP, WPA2, WPA3, evil twin, RADIUS.  OS & Workstation Hardening: BitLocker, UAC, AppLocker, patch management.  Mobile, Data & SOHO: MDM, NIST 800-88, degaussing, router hardening.

clues.clue: This type of control — which includes locks, bollards, and fences — works to PREVENT unauthorized physical access before it occurs.
clues.explain: Preventive controls stop a threat from happening. Locks, bollards, and perimeter fencing are classic preventive physical security measures.

clues.clue: CCTV cameras serve this DUAL control purpose: discouraging attackers from attempting a breach AND recording evidence after one occurs.
clues.response: What are deterrent and detective controls?
clues.explain: A visible camera deters would-be intruders (deterrent) and captures footage for post-incident investigation (detective). It is one of the few controls that fills both roles simultaneously.

clues.clue: This biometric factor — scanning the unique patterns of blood vessels at the back of the eye — is classified as 'something you are' and offers extremely high accuracy.
clues.explain: Retinal scans read the vascular pattern behind the eye; this pattern is unique to each individual and very difficult to spoof, making it one of the most accurate biometric identifiers.

clues.clue: An access-control vestibule uses two interlocking doors so that only one can open at a time, specifically to defeat this physical attack where an unauthorized person follows an authorized one through a secured entry.
clues.explain: Tailgating occurs when an attacker slips through a secured door immediately behind a legitimate badge-holder. A mantrap/vestibule forces each person to be independently authenticated before the second door opens.

clues.clue: Unlike wet-pipe sprinkler systems, this clean-agent fire suppression technology — such as FM-200 or Novec 1230 — suppresses fires in server rooms without damaging electronic equipment.
clues.explain: FM-200 and Novec 1230 are total-flooding agents that displace or chemically interrupt combustion without leaving water or residue. They are the preferred choice in data centers where water would destroy equipment.

clues.clue: Of the three pillars of the CIA triad, this one ensures that authorized users can reach systems and data when they need them.
clues.explain: Availability is the CIA triad property guaranteeing that systems and data are accessible to authorized users on demand. Denial-of-service attacks and hardware failures directly threaten availability.

clues.clue: Multi-factor authentication requires credentials from at least two DIFFERENT factor categories; combining a password with a PIN does NOT qualify because both belong to this single category.
clues.explain: Passwords and PINs are both 'something you know.' True MFA requires factors from two or more distinct categories — know, have, or are — so pairing two knowledge factors does not meet the definition.

clues.clue: In this access-control model, a DATA OWNER decides who can read or write to their files, and may freely share those permissions with others.
clues.explain: Under DAC the resource owner has full discretion to grant or revoke access. Most consumer operating systems use DAC by default, which is why file sharing is user-controlled.

clues.clue: Authentication and authorization are always performed in this order — a system must first verify WHO you are before it can decide WHAT you are allowed to do.
clues.explain: Authentication (verifying identity) must precede authorization (granting permissions). Granting access rights without first confirming identity would undermine the entire access-control framework.

clues.clue: Unlike symmetric encryption such as AES — which uses the same key to encrypt and decrypt — this encryption method uses a mathematically linked key PAIR, making it well-suited for secure key exchange.
clues.explain: Asymmetric algorithms use a public key to encrypt and a private key to decrypt (or vice versa for signatures). RSA is the most common example. The key-pair design solves the key-distribution problem that symmetric encryption faces.

clues.clue: This category of malware attack — consistently ranked the number-one initial attack vector in security studies — uses deceptive email messages to trick users into clicking malicious links or attachments.
clues.explain: Phishing emails impersonate trusted senders to steal credentials or deploy malware. It remains the most common entry point for breaches because it exploits human trust rather than technical vulnerabilities.

clues.clue: Unlike a virus, which requires a host file to spread, this type of malware is STANDALONE and self-replicates automatically across networks without any user action.
clues.explain: Worms propagate independently across network connections, consuming bandwidth and infecting hosts. The distinction from viruses is key: viruses need a carrier file and human action to spread; worms do not.

clues.clue: This advanced ransomware tactic goes beyond encrypting victim data — attackers ALSO exfiltrate the data and threaten to publish it unless a ransom is paid, creating two forms of leverage.
clues.explain: Double extortion means the attacker both encrypts the data (denying access) and steals it (threatening exposure). Even if victims restore from backups, the threat of public data release remains as a second ransom lever.

clues.clue: A threat actor plants malicious USB drives in a company parking lot hoping curious employees will plug them in — this social engineering technique is called this.
clues.explain: Baiting exploits human curiosity by leaving infected physical media (USB drives, SD cards) where targets will find them. Once inserted, the drive auto-runs malware or prompts credential theft.

clues.clue: This category of malware hides itself and other malicious processes from the operating system's normal detection mechanisms, often modifying kernel-level functions to stay invisible.
clues.explain: Rootkits operate at a privileged level — sometimes in the kernel — and intercept OS calls that would normally reveal their presence. This makes them extremely difficult to detect with standard antivirus tools that rely on OS-reported process lists.

clues.clue: This wireless security protocol, the current enterprise standard, uses AES-CCMP encryption and supports both a Personal (pre-shared key) mode and an Enterprise mode with RADIUS authentication.
clues.explain: WPA2 replaced the broken WEP and deprecated WPA-TKIP. Its use of AES in Counter Mode with CBC-MAC (CCMP) provides strong confidentiality and integrity. WPA2-Enterprise adds 802.1X port-based authentication via RADIUS.

clues.clue: This wireless attack creates a rogue access point with the same SSID as a legitimate network, tricking nearby devices into connecting to the attacker's equipment instead.
clues.response: What is an evil twin attack?
clues.explain: An evil twin mimics a known SSID so that client devices auto-associate with the attacker's AP. All traffic then passes through the attacker, enabling credential harvesting and man-in-the-middle interception.

clues.clue: Although commonly used on home routers to simplify device pairing, this feature should be DISABLED because its 8-digit PIN authentication is vulnerable to brute-force attack.
clues.explain: WPS uses a PIN that can be brute-forced in hours due to a design flaw (the PIN is verified in two halves). Security guidance universally recommends disabling WPS on all access points.

clues.clue: The 802.1X standard provides this function at the wireless (and wired) network edge — a client cannot pass any traffic until it has been authenticated by a back-end RADIUS server.
clues.response: What is port-based Network Access Control (NAC)?
clues.explain: 802.1X blocks the network port (physical or logical) until the supplicant proves identity to the authenticator, which forwards credentials to a RADIUS server. Only after approval does the port transition to an authorized state.

clues.clue: A weakness unique to WPA2 is that management frames — including deauthentication frames — are sent UNAUTHENTICATED, enabling this denial-of-service attack that forcibly disconnects clients from their access point.
clues.explain: Because WPA2 management frames lack encryption or authentication, any attacker can forge deauth frames to kick clients off the network. WPA3 addresses this with Management Frame Protection (MFP), which cryptographically authenticates management frames.

clues.clue: This built-in Windows security feature prompts the user for confirmation or administrator credentials whenever a process attempts to make changes that require elevated privileges.
clues.explain: UAC enforces the principle of least privilege by requiring explicit consent before privilege elevation. This limits the damage malware can do when running under a standard user account.

clues.clue: Windows Defender Firewall operates across three distinct profiles — Domain, Private, and this third profile — which applies the most restrictive rules when a device connects to an untrusted network such as a coffee-shop hotspot.
clues.explain: The Public profile blocks most inbound connections and disables network discovery. Windows automatically selects the appropriate profile based on network type, with Public being the most locked-down option for untrusted environments.

clues.clue: This Windows full-disk encryption feature stores the encryption key in a dedicated hardware chip on the motherboard, protecting data even if a laptop's hard drive is physically removed.
clues.explain: BitLocker encrypts the entire volume using AES. When paired with a Trusted Platform Module (TPM), the key is sealed to the hardware and released only when the boot environment is verified as unmodified, preventing offline attacks.

clues.clue: Rather than maintaining a list of BLOCKED software, AppLocker enforces this stronger security posture — only applications on an administrator-approved list are permitted to execute.
clues.explain: Whitelisting defaults to deny-all and permits only explicitly approved executables, scripts, and installers. This is far more effective than blacklisting because unknown or zero-day malware is blocked by default.

clues.clue: This Microsoft enterprise tool automatically rotates a UNIQUE local administrator password on each domain-joined workstation and stores it securely in Active Directory, eliminating the risk of a shared local-admin credential being used for lateral movement.
clues.response: What is LAPS (Local Administrator Password Solution)?
clues.explain: LAPS randomizes the built-in local administrator password on every managed machine on a configurable schedule. Because each machine has a different password, compromising one workstation's local admin account cannot be directly reused to authenticate to other machines.

clues.clue: The FIRST and most critical step in hardening any new SOHO router is performing this action, because factory credentials are publicly documented and are the number-one target for attackers.
clues.response: What is changing the default administrator credentials (username and password)?
clues.explain: Default credentials for every consumer router model are published online. Attackers scan for routers still using defaults; changing them immediately closes the most commonly exploited entry point.

clues.clue: An enterprise Mobile Device Management platform can send this command to a lost or stolen corporate device, wiping all data without requiring physical possession of the hardware.
clues.explain: MDM agents running on enrolled devices listen for management commands. A remote wipe command triggers a full factory reset, protecting sensitive corporate data even when the device cannot be physically recovered.

clues.clue: According to NIST SP 800-88, this data sanitization level — the lowest of three — involves overwriting media with known patterns and is suitable for storage devices that will be reused within the same organization.
clues.explain: NIST SP 800-88 defines three levels: Clear (overwrite, suitable for internal reuse), Purge (more thorough techniques like cryptographic erase or ATA Secure Erase), and Destroy (physical destruction). Clear is the baseline minimum.

clues.clue: Degaussing — exposing magnetic media to a powerful magnetic field — effectively destroys data on traditional hard disk drives, but is completely INEFFECTIVE on this modern storage type.
clues.response: What is an SSD (solid-state drive) or flash storage?
clues.explain: SSDs store data in NAND flash cells, not magnetic platters, so a magnetic field has no effect on them. NIST SP 800-88 prescribes ATA Secure Erase or cryptographic erase (destroying the encryption key) to sanitize SSDs.

clues.clue: This process — installing mobile apps from sources OUTSIDE the official platform app store — bypasses the store's vetting and code-signing checks, significantly increasing the risk of installing malware.
clues.explain: App stores apply automated and manual security reviews before publishing apps. Sideloading circumvents these controls, allowing unsigned or malicious APKs (Android) or IPAs (iOS via enterprise certificates) to run. MDM policies commonly prohibit sideloading on managed devices.
